basic_info: Patient is Abigail, presenting with right knee pain affecting her running. Visit time is unspecified. Major symptom is knee pain.
present_illness: The patient reports that the right knee pain began a few months ago and has progressively worsened with running. The pain typically aches towards the end of the day, especially after prolonged standing. The patient notes that applying ice and taking ibuprofen provides temporary relief. The patient mentions noticing a little bit of fluid under the knee, which was mentioned during a prior exam. The pain is more of a dull ache, especially on the outside of my right knee, and it gets worse towards the end of the day after being on my feet. I don't have any numbness or tingling, but the fluid under the knee seems to be there consistently, and it's been linked to running and being active throughout the day.
past_history: No specific prior injuries reported. Family history of joint-related conditions is unknown.
physical_exam: The physical examination revealed a small amount of effusion in the right knee without redness or swelling. There was no tenderness or instability noted during the examination. Range of motion and movement of the leg were not painful.
aux_exam: X-rays were taken, showing normal joint spaces with no sign of fracture or arthritis. MRI or ultrasound imaging of the right knee has not been performed yet. No blood tests, including inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR, CRP) or autoimmune panels (e.g., RF, ANA), have been performed yet.
